key_insight: Variantscape uses large language models to map literature-reported links between genetic variants, cancer types, and treatments at scale.
clinical_relevance: The resource may support precision oncology research and molecular tumour board preparation, but extracted associations do not establish treatment efficacy.
method: Screen biomedical abstracts for gene mentions.
Combine traditional NLP and LLMs to extract and standardise variant–treatment–cancer associations.
Use LLMs to verify associations against abstract text and build a searchable graph.
evidence_signal: Of 886,195 gene-containing articles, 37,895 mentioned all three entity types; LLM verification confirmed at least one association in 35,224 papers, yielding 44,644 verified graph edges.
watch_item: Verification was LLM-based and limited to abstracts; the supplied abstract reports no independent expert-validation metrics.
paper_title: Variantscape: Retrospective Study of Large Language Model-Based Extraction of Variant-Treatment-Cancer Associations from Published Oncology Abstracts
